implementation_notes: Python absorbs the two-class Essence structure into init-time validation of an immutable class: a @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) declares every compulsory property as a mandatory field (no default, so the generated __init__ refuses to omit it), and __post_init__ - called at the end of the generated __init__ - is the single validation routine that raises ValueError naming all violated invariants before the instance can reach the caller; keyword arguments replace the Essence's setter permutations, and a classmethod factory such as Contract.from_payload() takes the Essence role when values must be derived or checked before construction. attrs generalizes the same idiom with field(validator=...), running per-attribute and cross-attribute checks at init and re-validating on assignment for @define/@frozen classes. The classic hand-written Essence/CreationTarget pair stays justified when creation is initiated by clients the designer cannot trust or one Essence must stamp out many targets with shared values - Python has no private constructors or friend classes, so it cannot seal __init__ the way Java package-private or C++ friend declarations do.
pitfalls: frozen=True only emulates immutability - the dataclasses documentation is explicit that truly immutable Python objects are impossible: object.__setattr__(obj, 'customer', ...) bypasses the freeze, and a held list/dict field stays mutable (shallow freeze); use tuple/frozenset for compulsory collections.

__post_init__ is skipped when the class defines its own __init__ or a field is declared init=False - validation silently disappears, the Python face of the classic 'bypassing Essence' trap; keep the rules in one __post_init__ or a shared function every construction path calls.

The @dataclass decorator raises ValueError for unhashable (mutable) defaults such as [], and an eq+frozen class gains __hash__, so a wrongly validated object can already be used as a dict/set key and corrupt the mapping - validate before storing, matching the pattern's dictionary-key/database-index context.

Unlike attrs (@define/@frozen re-run validators on assignment), plain dataclasses never re-validate after construction; mutating a compulsory property of a non-frozen class passes silently - choose attrs.frozen when post-creation immutability must actually be enforced.

Raising inside __init__ makes invalid objects unconstructible (EAFP is the accepted idiom), but interactive form feedback is better served by a validate(payload) helper run before construction - the Python analogue of Essence.validateParameters(); exception-driven control flow per field is the smell the early-feedback method exists to avoid.
